text: Every filter you build lives in one single pane, and applies at one of three distinct levels. Let's walk through all of it, because this is the control that shapes what every visual on your report actually shows.

Visual-level affects only the one visual it's attached to. Page-level affects every visual on the current page. Report-level affects every visual across every page of the entire report. Power BI automatically creates a visual-level filter card the moment you add a field to a visual — drag any other field into the Filters pane yourself to add more, at whichever level you drop it. And any viewer, even without opening that pane, can hover over a visual and select the filter icon to see a read-only summary of exactly what's affecting it — no editing required, just visibility.

Lock a filter, and viewers can see it but can't change it. Hide it entirely, and they can't see it at all — useful for data-cleanup filters, like excluding nulls or test rows, that a viewer has no reason to know about, let alone adjust themselves. You can even format the pane itself to match your report's look, with separate colors for applied versus available filter cards.

And on larger reports, turn on a single Apply button under Query reduction options — viewers can make several filter changes first, and nothing re-queries the report until they actually select Apply. One small setting, a genuinely outsized effect on how fast a large report feels to use.
Next: cross filtering and visual interactions — how selecting one data point on the page actually ripples through every other visual around it.
